prompt: Create a simple square-ish children’s picture-book illustration of a polar bear standing on a large floating ice floe in the Arctic Ocean. The animal is shown in side view facing left, occupying most of the frame, with a stout rounded body, short natural neck, four legs visible, small rounded ears, tiny tail, cream-white fur, thick black cartoon outline, and a stern determined face with round eyes, black nose, and flat mouth. Use a naive hand-painted acrylic or oil-pastel style with visible brush strokes, slightly uneven edges, bold black contours, and flat bright colors. The setting is a vivid cyan-blue sky above a dark blue ocean horizon, with exactly 2 simple white blocky clouds in the sky, one at upper left and one at upper right. Include exactly 6 smaller floating ice chunks in the water around the main floe: 3 on the left side, 3 on the right side. The main ice floe should be large, jagged, white on top with light-blue shaded sides, filling the bottom third of the image. Keep the composition playful and graphic, like a handmade children’s book page, with no text, no watermark, no photorealism, and no extra animals.
